quotes.text: The FCC repealed the Fairness Doctrine 4–0 on Aug 4, 1987, ending 38 years of mandated on-air rebuttal.
By 1993 the Rush Limbaugh Show ran on 650+ stations and drew 20 million listeners a week.
Newt Gingrich's 1990 GOPAC memo gave candidates 64 words to use about Democrats: 'sick,' 'pathetic,' 'traitors,' 'destroy.'
Drudge posted Newsweek's killed Lewinsky story at 11:32 PM on Jan 17, 1998. Cable picked it up by sunrise.
Fox News Channel launched October 7, 1996, in 17 million homes — by 2002 it was the top-rated cable news network.
The Christian Coalition distributed 33 million voter guides in churches on the Sunday before the 1992 election.
Roger Ailes drafted a memo to Nixon in 1970 proposing a 'GOP TV news' network. He waited 26 years and built it.
Pat Robertson's '700 Club' reached 7 million households by 1988 — and ran the largest direct-mail political list in America.
Limbaugh callers signed off with 'dittos' instead of agreeing in detail. The chorus identified itself by refusing to argue.
